query: What features can be extracted to train a model to predict a review's score?

per_column.name: overall_sentiment_polarity
per_column.rationale: Overall sentiment of the review is effectively a near-deterministic restatement of the star score; positive/negative polarity is what the score encodes. Predicting score from overall sentiment is circular leakage.

per_column.name: review_tone_extremity
per_column.rationale: Strongly_positive vs strongly_negative tone maps almost directly onto 5 vs 1 stars; it is a graded restatement of the score's affect and leaks the outcome.

per_column.name: repurchase_intent
per_column.rationale: Repurchase intent is correlated with satisfaction but is a distinct downstream disposition, not a restatement of the star value; it can carry residual signal while lying outside the score itself. Borderline but defensible as a predictor.

per_column.name: taste_flavor_satisfaction
per_column.rationale: Satisfaction with the product is the very sentiment the score expresses; highly_satisfied/dissatisfied is essentially the score under another name for food items.

per_column.name: flavor_strength_perception
per_column.rationale: Whether flavor is balanced/too_weak/too_strong is a specific attribute perception, not directly the overall score; it can carry signal without being a restatement of satisfaction.

per_column.name: bitterness_presence
per_column.rationale: Presence of a specific attribute (bitterness) is an objective-ish feature that only weakly and indirectly relates to score; it is a legitimate outside predictor, though low-variance (2.4% true).

per_column.name: texture_satisfaction
per_column.rationale: Framed as satisfaction (positive/negative/mixed), this restates the evaluative sentiment the score captures, just scoped to texture; it leaks the outcome affect.

per_column.name: product_quality_judgment
per_column.rationale: Exceeds/meets/below expectations is an overall evaluative judgment nearly isomorphic to the star rating; it restates the score.

per_column.name: product_efficacy
per_column.rationale: Positive_effect/negative_effect/no_effect is an evaluative satisfaction judgment about whether the product worked, which maps onto the score; it leaks the outcome.

per_column.name: ease_of_use
per_column.rationale: Easy/moderate/difficult is a specific usability attribute distinct from the overall rating; it can plausibly influence score without restating it.

per_column.name: product_category
per_column.rationale: Category (coffee, snack, pet food, etc.) is an objective covariate outside the score that can carry weak predictive signal via category-level rating tendencies; not leakage.

per_column.name: usage_context
per_column.rationale: Context of use (gift, pet, cooking) is an objective circumstance independent of the rating value; a legitimate outside feature with plausible signal.

per_column.name: expectation_match
per_column.rationale: Exceeded/met/not_met is an overall evaluative outcome essentially equivalent to the star rating; it restates the score and leaks.

per_column.name: novelty_value
per_column.rationale: Whether the product is perceived as novel is a descriptive attribute distinct from satisfaction; can carry weak signal without restating the score.

per_column.name: reviewer_expertise_signal
per_column.rationale: Reviewer type (expert/first-time/regular) is a covariate about the author, outside the outcome, and can carry predictive signal about rating behavior.

per_column.name: review_specificity_level
per_column.rationale: Detail/specificity of the text is a stylistic feature independent of the score's polarity; a legitimate outside predictor, albeit weak.

judge.rationale: Many of the strongest-looking columns (overall_sentiment_polarity, review_tone_extremity, taste_flavor_satisfaction, texture_satisfaction, product_quality_judgment, product_efficacy, expectation_match) are evaluative satisfaction/sentiment judgments that essentially restate the star score and constitute leakage — a model using them would trivially recover the outcome rather than genuinely predict it. The legitimate outside predictors (category, usage_context, reviewer_expertise, specificity, ease_of_use, flavor_strength, bitterness, novelty, repurchase_intent) are real covariates but individually carry only weak signal about score and several are dominated by 'not_applicable'. As a set they provide modest genuine predictive leverage beyond the original columns, heavily contaminated by leakage-prone features.
